memos.risk:
Risk officer view: the desk should lean toward refusing this one.

Ticket size: if the desk buys at all, $5 is the ceiling. Pool depth of 79 SOL is thin and the 15-minute volume (~$2,800) is small relative to a $20 ticket plus 1.4-5.1% round-trip cost.

Stop: 20%, the tight end, given the 32% drawdown already seen and no evidence of a floor.

Hold: 15 minutes maximum.

Refusal triggers, any one sufficient: the launch bot and top-5 buyers holding 64% of early buys point to a concentrated, probably operator-driven launch, with an unresolved class and missing bundle and completer data. Sell-to-buy of 0.61 in the first two minutes is weak. Name and symbol are null, so the metadata is unverifiable. Graduation is unknown. I'd also refuse if the 30-second execution lag could let the price move past the stop before the order lands.

My recommendation is to skip. The known data doesn't show an edge, and a skipped coin costs nothing.
memos.scout:
The case for buying is thin. The strongest point is recent net buying: last 15 minutes show 13.62 SOL bought against 10.1 SOL sold (net +3.52 SOL), 11 buyers, and a +8.7% return off the window's low, with about $2.8k volume. Pool depth of 79 SOL is reasonable for a $20 ticket, and the coin is alive, not an airdrop factory (no dump seen).

Against that: the coin is 31.8% below its 30-minute high, and the first two minutes after graduation were heavily sell-pressured (sell/buy ratio 0.61) with the top five buyers taking 64% of early flow and a launch bot present. Those are classic exit-liquidity signatures, and the curve concentration data is missing, so we can't rule out a concentrated holder. Name and symbol are null, so there is no visible community or metadata signal. A 30-minute bounce from a deep drawdown is the pattern most likely to fail, and the 1.4-5.1% round-trip cost means the bounce has to clear that hurdle first.

Verdict: no strong honest case. Skip.
memos.skeptic: Most likely loss path: insider distribution into the recent bounce. The first two minutes show a launch bot present, 25 early buyers, and a top-5 buyer share of 64%, with sell-to-buy at 0.61, so early size is concentrated and already partly exiting. Over the last 15 minutes sellers (8) are unloading 10.1 SOL against 13.6 SOL of buys, and the coin is already 31.8% below its 30-minute high after a -13.2% 30-minute return. The +8.7% bounce sits on thin 15-minute volume (about $2.8k) against a 79 SOL pool, so a round trip at 1.4-5.1% fees could erase a small move. Bundle share, completer share, and graduation timing are all unknown, and the class is UNRESOLVED, so there's no operator backing to lean on. Name and symbol are null, which removes any metadata check. Skip.
